Rajveer & Ors. Cnr No: Dlse0100-9557-2018 1. Lalit (minor) S/o Smt. Bharti R/o H.No.125, Dholagarh(79), Palwal-121102, Haryana .....Petitioner Versus 1. Rajveer Singh S/o Sh. Bhagwan Singh R/o Nagla Turkiya Pani ki tanki ke pas, Makkhanpur, Firozabad, U.P. ............Driver/Respondent no.1 2. Manish Bansal S/o Sh. Bishan Kumar Bansal R/o 35 Hanuman Road, Firozabad, U.P. ............Owner/Respondent no.2 3. Royal Sundaram General Insurance Company Ltd. Unit no.801A, 8th floor, Devika Tower, Nehru Place, New Delhi. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Mact No.1057/18 Lalit v. Rajveer & Ors. P.No. 1 Of 22 ss Charu by Charu Gupta Gupta 2025.04.21 Date: 16:04:48 +0530 Date of accident : 03.06.2018 Result of accident : Grievous/permanent disability Date of filing of Petition : 13.11.2018 Date of Decision : 21.04.2025 Award 1.
texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Lalit (17 years) suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. Brief facts of the case are that on 03.06.2018 at about 8 a.m. petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing no. HR-30K-0264 driven by one Saurabh. When they were coming towards Village Dholagarh, a speeding car Honda Amaze bearing vehicle no. UP-83Ae-5885 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) suddenly hit the motorcycle of victim. Due to the impact, the petitioner as well as the driver of motorcycle fell on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Both the victims were removed to the nearest Government hospital from where they were after referred to Delhi Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.0409/18 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC PS Camp Palwal, Distt-Palwal. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed u/s 279/337/338 of IPC before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no. 2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. MACT NO.1057/18 Lalit v. Rajveer & Ors. P.No. 2 Of 22 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA No Written statement or reply filed on behalf of Respondent no.1 & 2 despite opportunity. 6. Respondent no.3/insurance company filed his reply denying the occurrence of the accident and refuting the allegations of rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no.1/driver. It is stated that as per petition, the FIR has been lodged 8 days after the alleged incident and thus the claim be declined as suspicious. 7. Vide order dated 16.08.2021, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 03.06.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-83AE-5885 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Whether the injured is entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. 8. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/injured examined himself as PW-1. To prove his claim, petitioner /Lalit led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the claim petition. He stated that on 03.06.2018 at about 8 a.m. he was going from Dholgarh Village, Haryana to Camp Palwal on motorcycle with his friend namely Saurabh and the Lalit vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121913945/ 2 motorcycle was being driven by his friend with due care and normal speed. He was pillion rider. As soon as they reached Dholagarh Mod, Palwal Haryana, all of a sudden a speeding car bearing no. UP-83AE-5885 came from Hodal Haryana side in a rash and MACT NO.1057/18 Lalit v. Rajveer & Ors. P.No. 3 Of 22 ss CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.04.21 16:04:57 +0530 negligent manner and hit the motorcycle from behind with great force. Due to the accident, petitioner along with his friend fell on the road and sustained multiple grievous injuries. PW-1 further deposed that father of the injured Saurabh was present at the spot at the time of accident and he immediately noted down the registration number of the offending vehicle and took both victims to Civil Hospital, Palwal, Haryana. He further deposed that later he was shifted /referred to JPN Apex Trauma Center, New Delhi due to his critical condition. Due to the accident petitioner sustained 11% disability in relation to both lower limbs. He deposed that he is unmarried and was studying in class 12th prior to the accident. PW-1 deposed that he spent about Rs.2,50,000/- on his treatment and is still under the medical treatment. He further deposed that he hired an attendant for 12 months and paid about Rs.12,000/- per month. He relied upon his Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1, Academic documents as Ex.PW1/2, medical treatment records along with certified copy of discharge summary as Ex.PW1/3, original medical bills as Ex.PW1/4, disability certificate as Ex.PW1/5, certified copy of MLR as Ex.PW1/6, certified copy of FIR as Ex.PW1/7, certified copy of DL of driver of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/8, copy of insurance police of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/10, copy of site plan as Ex.PW1/11, copy of mechanical inspection of offending vehicle as Ex.PW1/12, copy of statement of u/s 161 Cr.P.C. as Ex.PW1/13 and copy of chargesheet along with documents as Ex.PW1/14. He was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/Respondent no.3. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. P.No. 4 Of 22 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Final arguments in detail were addressed by learned counsel for the claimants/petitioners and by counsel for respondent no. 3. It is argued on behalf of the claimants that the accident was caused by respondent no.1 by driving the offending truck in a rash and negligent manner. 12. In the present case, petitioner/injured has examined himself as PW-1 wherein he has testified in detail, the date and manner of accident on the lines of petition. He has categorically deposed that the accident was a collision from the front of the offending vehicle. Despite cross examining PW-1, no suggestion denying the occurrence of the accident on the part of respondent no.1 has been put by the insurance company. Respondent no.1 /driver and respondent no.2/owner of the offending vehicle have also not taken any defence by filing any written statement or contesting the claim of the petitioner by cross examining him.
texts.arguments: It is argued that since respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle, which is owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no. 3, respondents are liable to compensate the claimant for the injury sustained grievous injury. Lalit vs Rajveer Singh on 21 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121913945/ 3 On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of the insurance company that there is no eye witness to the accident and the eye witness examined by the petitioner has been planted. It is argued that the petitioner was driving without a valid driving licence and without a helmet and as such is liable to deduction on account of contributory negligence. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj MACT NO.1057/18 Lalit v. Rajveer & Ors. Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 20. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
